page.standard_overview: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) is an uncommon etiology of stroke characterized by thrombosis within the dural venous sinuses (superior sagittal, transverse, sigmoid) or deep cerebral veins. Affecting predominantly young adults and women, pathogenesis involves an interplay of prothrombotic risk factors, including oral contraceptives, pregnancy, puerperium, thrombophilias, and local head/neck infections. Clinical presentation typically features progressive or acute headache (often worse with recumbency or Valsalva), papilledema, seizures, and focal neurological deficits. European and international guidelines endorse full-dose anticoagulation (LMWH or unfractionated heparin) as the definitive acute first-line treatment, even in the presence of baseline venous hemorrhagic infarction.

page.standard_overview: After initial parenteral anticoagulation, patients with cerebral venous thrombosis usually transition to an oral anticoagulant to prevent recurrent cerebral or systemic venous thromboembolism; venous recanalization varies and is a monitored outcome rather than the sole treatment goal. Historically managed with vitamin K antagonists (warfarin, INR target 2.0-3.0), the small randomized RESPECT-CVT trial (dabigatran) and the international ACTION-CVT cohort suggest that direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) offer comparable recanalization and recurrent venous thromboembolism prevention, with lower major bleeding in the ACTION-CVT cohort. Recommended treatment duration spans 3 to 6 months for provoked CVT with a resolved risk factor, and 6 to 12 months or indefinite for unprovoked cases or high-risk thrombophilia.

page.standard_overview: Cervical cancer is almost universally caused by persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infection, primarily genotypes 16 and 18, which drive oncogenic progression via E6 and E7 oncoproteins inactivating p53 and retinoblastoma (Rb) tumor suppressor pathways. Primary prevention relies on prophylactic HPV vaccination, while secondary prevention has evolved to primary hrHPV testing with reflex cytology. Clinical staging follows the updated 2018 FIGO system, which formally incorporates imaging (MRI, PET/CT) and pathological lymph node status. Management ranges from fertility-sparing conization or trachelectomy and radical hysterectomy in selected early disease to concurrent platinum-based chemoradiotherapy with brachytherapy for locally advanced disease; pembrolizumab plus platinum-based chemotherapy, with or without bevacizumab, improves survival in eligible persistent, recurrent or metastatic disease.

page.standard_overview: Degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM)—formerly termed cervical spondylotic myelopathy—is the most prevalent cause of spinal cord dysfunction and acquired spastic quadriparesis in adults worldwide. Pathophysiology involves chronic static mechanical cord compression (osteophytes, disc herniation, ligamentum flavum hypertrophy, ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament) compounded by dynamic microvascular ischemia during neck flexion and extension. Clinical presentation features clumsy, numb hands, loss of fine motor dexterity, gait instability, and classic upper motor neuron signs (hyperreflexia, Hoffmann sign, inverted supinator jerk, Babinski). Clinical guidelines strongly endorse timely anterior or posterior surgical decompression for moderate-to-severe or progressive myelopathy to halt neurological decline and optimize functional recovery.

page.standard_overview: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT) represents the most common inherited peripheral neuropathy, exhibiting significant genetic heterogeneity. CMT1A, the predominant CMT1 subtype and roughly 40-50% of CMT overall, is an autosomal dominant demyelinating neuropathy caused by a 1.4-megabase chromosome 17p11.2 duplication containing PMP22. Electrophysiologically, CMT1A is characterized by uniform, symmetric nerve conduction slowing (median motor nerve conduction velocity <38 m/s) without conduction block or temporal dispersion. Clinical presentation features childhood or adolescent onset of distal muscle wasting ('inverted champagne bottle' legs), bilateral foot drop, pes cavus, hammer toes, sensory ataxia, and generalized areflexia.

standard_knowledge.claim: Pharmacovigilance and registry data demonstrate that ICI-associated myocarditis has a case fatality rate exceeding 40% with combination immunotherapy (anti-PD-1 plus anti-CTLA-4), presenting early with arrhythmias and conduction block.

Over 90% of patients with ICI myocarditis have elevated cardiac troponin T/I; normal left ventricular ejection fraction on echocardiography is common (present in ~50%), meaning preserved LVEF does not rule out severe, fulminant disease.

page.standard_overview: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) myocarditis is an uncommon (incidence roughly 0.1 to 1%) but life-threatening immune-related adverse event (irAE) associated with anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, and anti-CTLA-4 therapies. Fatality rates approach 25% to 50%, peaking with dual combination regimens (nivolumab plus ipilimumab). ICI myocarditis is a T-cell-mediated inflammatory myotoxicity with myocardial lymphocytic and macrophage infiltration; it often presents early after treatment initiation and can cause heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias, conduction block or cardiogenic shock, although milder presentations also occur. Myocarditis can overlap with skeletal myositis and myasthenia-gravis-like disease ('triple M' syndrome), a high-risk combination that warrants assessment for respiratory-muscle involvement. Management requires prompt ICI discontinuation and high-dose corticosteroids for clinically significant myocarditis, with early specialist escalation for severe or refractory disease; abatacept-based strategies are promising, and any later ICI rechallenge requires highly individualized expert review.

page.standard_overview: Chemotherapy extravasation—the accidental leakage of antineoplastic agents from vascular structures into perivascular and subcutaneous tissue—is an oncologic nursing and medical emergency capable of causing severe soft-tissue necrosis, tendon sloughing, and long-term functional limb impairment. Antineoplastic agents are categorized by tissue injury potential: vesicants (DNA-binding agents like anthracyclines [doxorubicin] and non-DNA binding agents like vinca alkaloids [vincristine]), irritants, and non-vesicants. Emergency management protocol mandates immediately stopping the infusion, aspirating residual drug through the cannula, avoiding line flushing, and limb elevation. Antidote and thermal management are agent-specific: intravenous dexrazoxane for anthracycline extravasation, local hyaluronidase with warming for vinca alkaloids, cooling for anthracyclines, and topical DMSO only for selected agents under an applicable protocol rather than generically for 'others'.

page.standard_overview: Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) is one of the most feared and debilitating adverse effects of cancer chemotherapy, directly impairing nutritional status, treatment adherence, and overall quality of life. Pathophysiologically, CINV is classified into distinct temporal phases: acute nausea/vomiting (occurring within 0 to 24 hours of administration, mediated by enterochromaffin serotonin 5-HT3 release), delayed nausea/vomiting (occurring from 24 to 120 hours post-chemotherapy, driven by central area postrema substance P and neurokinin-1 [NK1] receptor activation), and anticipatory nausea (a conditioned psychological response). Evidence-based prophylaxis is determined by the inherent emetogenicity of the regimen (highly emetogenic [HEC], moderately emetogenic [MEC], low, or minimal) rather than treating symptoms reactively.

The differential pharmacology of antiemetics aligns with neurochemical pathways: 5-HT3 antagonists block acute serotonin release, while NK1 antagonists block delayed central substance P signaling, yielding synergistic emesis suppression.

page.standard_overview: Prophylaxis for highly emetogenic chemotherapy, including cisplatin, dacarbazine and anthracycline-cyclophosphamide regimens, commonly uses a four-drug regimen comprising an NK1 receptor antagonist, a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist, dexamethasone and olanzapine. The landmark phase 3 trial by Navari et al. established that adding olanzapine (atypical antipsychotic targeting dopamine D2, serotonin 5-HT2c/5-HT3, and histamine H1 receptors) to standard triplet therapy significantly elevates complete response rates for nausea prevention in both acute and delayed phases. Current international guidelines from ASCO and ESMO endorse this quadruple combination: a neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptor antagonist (aprepitant or fosaprepitant), a 5-HT3 receptor antagonist (ondansetron, granisetron, or palonosetron), dexamethasone, and olanzapine.

page.standard_overview: Antiemetic prophylaxis in moderately emetogenic chemotherapy (MEC)—including regimens based on carboplatin, oxaliplatin, irinotecan, and cyclophosphamide—focuses on robust control of delayed emesis using innovative pharmacological formulations. Second-generation 5-HT3 receptor antagonists, specifically palonosetron, exhibit high receptor binding affinity, an extended plasma half-life (~40 hours), and unique receptor internalization properties that confer prolonged antiemetic action across both acute and delayed phases. Oral NEPA combines netupitant and palonosetron in one pre-chemotherapy dose to block NK1 and 5-HT3 pathways and simplify prophylaxis; it is used with dexamethasone when indicated, and breakthrough or refractory CINV can still require additional treatment.

page.standard_overview: Assessment of acute chest pain in the emergency department (ED) requires rapid, protocolized triage to rule in or rule out life-threatening cardiopulmonary emergencies while avoiding unnecessary hospital admissions. Validated risk stratification tools, such as the HEART score and EDACS, guide downstream non-invasive functional or anatomical coronary testing (CCTA) in intermediate-risk cohorts.

page.standard_overview: Beyond acute coronary syndromes, emergency evaluation of acute chest pain mandates rapid, systematic exclusion of the five other life-threatening non-ACS chest pain etiologies: acute aortic dissection, acute pulmonary embolism (PE), tension pneumothorax, esophageal rupture (Boerhaave syndrome), and cardiac tamponade. Using bedside physical examination, targeted clinical decision rules (e.g., Wells score for PE, ADD-RS for aortic dissection), point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), and protocolized hs-cTn pathways, clinicians distinguish benign musculoskeletal or esophageal chest pain from critical vascular catastrophes. The HEART Pathway combines the HEART score with serial troponin measurements to identify patients for early discharge; randomized evaluation found less downstream cardiac testing, a 12-hour shorter stay and 21.3% more early discharges without 30-day MACE among patients identified for early discharge.

standard_knowledge.claim: Long-term prospective cohorts demonstrate that 30% to 50% of Chikungunya patients develop persistent, chronic debilitating arthralgia or erosive arthritis lasting up to 36 months following acute infection.

Chronic Chikungunya arthritis closely mimics seronegative rheumatoid arthritis, characterized by symmetric small-joint synovitis, elevated inflammatory markers, and response to disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs).

Zika virus infection is typically mild and self-limiting (lasting 2-7 days with fever, rash, conjunctivitis, and arthralgia), but is uniquely associated with Guillain-Barré syndrome and severe congenital microcephaly.

page.standard_overview: Chikungunya and Zika viruses are Aedes aegypti- and Aedes albopictus-transmitted arboviruses; chikungunya characteristically causes prominent arthralgia and chronic rheumatologic disease, whereas Zika arthralgia is generally milder and shorter-lived. Acute Chikungunya infection is defined by high fevers, diffuse maculopapular exanthem, and severe, excruciating, symmetric polyarthralgia and tenosynovitis predominantly involving the wrists, hands, and ankles ('chikungunya' translates as 'that which bends up'). Crucially, in 30% to 50% of patients, arthropathy persists for months to years, mimicking seronegative rheumatoid arthritis or spondyloarthritis. Zika infection is often milder, with transient maculopapular rash, low-grade fever, non-purulent conjunctivitis and arthralgia, but it is notably associated with Guillain-Barré syndrome and congenital Zika syndrome, including microcephaly after maternal infection.

page.standard_overview: Recurrent wheezing during preschool years (age <6) is exceptionally prevalent, occurring in up to one-third of all children. The Tucson Children's Respiratory Study described transient early wheeze associated with reduced premorbid airway function and no increased atopy, persistent wheeze associated with maternal asthma and allergic features, and late-onset wheeze beginning after age 3; these groups vary in prognosis and are not interchangeable with later asthma phenotypes. Clinically, preschool wheezing is pragmatically categorized into episodic (viral) wheeze and multi-trigger wheeze (wheezing triggered by viral infections as well as exercise, cold air, laughing, or crying). Recognizing preschool wheeze patterns can guide individualized treatment trials and follow-up, but phenotypes overlap and change over time; inhaled corticosteroids should be continued only when there is clear clinical benefit rather than prescribed or withheld solely from a phenotype label.

page.standard_overview: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) encompasses a biologically and anatomically diverse group of aggressive epithelial malignancies arising from biliary tract epithelium. Classified anatomically into intrahepatic (iCCA), perihilar (pCCA, Klatskin tumor, comprising 50-60% of cases), and distal (dCCA, 20-30%), each exhibits distinct molecular landscapes, clinical presentations, and surgical resectability criteria. Prominent predisposing conditions include primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), choledochal cysts, hepatolithiasis, chronic viral hepatitis, and liver fluke infestations (Clonorchis sinensis). Perihilar and distal cholangiocarcinoma commonly present with painless obstructive jaundice, dark urine, pale stools and pruritus, whereas intrahepatic disease may instead cause right-upper-quadrant discomfort, weight loss or no early symptoms. Contrast-enhanced MRI with MRCP is a key modality for assessing biliary obstruction, ductal anatomy and local tumor extent, while multiphasic CT, endoscopic evaluation and tissue sampling are selected according to anatomical subtype and the diagnostic question. Curative-intent treatment includes complete R0 resection for resectable cholangiocarcinoma; carefully selected patients with unresectable perihilar tumors may instead be eligible for neoadjuvant chemoradiation followed by liver transplantation under a specialized protocol.

In the landmark ABC-02 phase 3 trial, gemcitabine plus cisplatin significantly improved median overall survival compared to gemcitabine alone (11.7 vs 8.1 months, HR 0.64) in advanced biliary tract cancer.

The phase 3 TOPAZ-1 trial demonstrated that adding durvalumab (anti-PD-L1) to gemcitabine and cisplatin significantly prolonged overall survival (HR 0.80) and progression-free survival, establishing chemo-immunotherapy as the preferred first-line standard.

In the phase 3 ClarIDHy trial, the oral mutant-IDH1 inhibitor ivosidenib significantly improved progression-free survival (HR 0.37) and preserved quality of life in patients with previously treated IDH1-mutated advanced cholangiocarcinoma.

In the randomized BILCAP study, adjuvant capecitabine for 8 cycles (6 months) following curative-intent surgical resection significantly prolonged median overall survival (53 vs 36 months in per-protocol analysis, HR 0.75), defining the adjuvant standard.

page.standard_overview: Systemic pharmacotherapy for advanced, unresectable, and metastatic biliary tract cancer (cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder cancer) has evolved dramatically from cytotoxic chemotherapy alone to biomarker-driven precision oncology and immunotherapy. The landmark ABC-02 trial established cisplatin plus gemcitabine as foundational first-line therapy. Recently, the randomized phase 3 TOPAZ-1 trial demonstrated that adding the anti-PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor durvalumab to gemcitabine/cisplatin significantly prolongs overall survival, establishing a new global standard of care. Molecular profiling can identify actionable subsets of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements can be treated with FGFR inhibitors such as pemigatinib or futibatinib, and previously treated IDH1-mutant disease benefits from ivosidenib, which improved progression-free survival in ClarIDHy. Adjuvant capecitabine for 6 months represents standard care post-curative resection (BILCAP).

page.standard_overview: Choledocholithiasis refers to the presence of gallstones within the common bile duct (CBD), occurring in 10% to 20% of patients with symptomatic cholelithiasis. The American Society for Gastrointestinal Endoscopy (ASGE) guidelines stratify patients into high (>50%), intermediate (10-50%), and low (<10%) probability tiers based on clinical, laboratory, and transabdominal ultrasound findings. ASGE 2019 lists a CBD stone on ultrasound, ascending cholangitis, and total bilirubin >4 mg/dL with a dilated CBD as high-risk criteria that generally proceed to therapeutic ERCP; however, their specificity is imperfect, and EUS-first assessment can avoid diagnostic ERCP in selected patients without cholangitis, particularly those meeting only the bilirubin-plus-dilation criterion. Intermediate-risk patients usually undergo further evaluation with MRCP or EUS rather than diagnostic ERCP; MRCP is non-invasive, whereas EUS is an endoscopic minimally invasive test, and confirming stones before ERCP can reduce unnecessary procedures and adverse-event exposure.

page.standard_overview: Acute ascending cholangitis is a life-threatening infection of the biliary tract resulting from biliary stasis and elevated intraductal pressure, most frequently triggered by an impacted common bile duct stone. Acute cholangitis classically presents with Charcot's triad of fever, jaundice and right-upper-quadrant pain, or Reynolds' pentad when hypotension and confusion are added; TG18 stratifies severity into Grade I (mild), Grade II (moderate) and Grade III (severe, with organ dysfunction). Initial treatment includes prompt resuscitation and early intravenous antimicrobials, with biliary drainage determined by severity and response: mild cases often respond without drainage, moderate cases require early drainage, and severe cases require drainage after initial respiratory and circulatory support; definitive stone treatment may be deferred until the patient improves. Grade III acute cholangitis requires biliary drainage as soon as possible after respiratory and circulatory stabilization, although drainage timing is only one component of management and does not by itself dictate survival.

overview_support.note: TG18: "AC occurs when biliary stenosis, due to various benign causes (often bile duct stones)... results in cholestasis and biliary infection", raising intrabiliary pressure.

TG18: "Early diagnosis, early biliary drainage and/or treatment for etiology, and antimicrobial administration are fundamental treatment for acute cholangitis"; non-responders to initial medical treatment need drainage.
TG18/TG13: lower 30-day mortality with early or urgent drainage only in Grade II; no difference in Grade I or III, so drainage timing does not by itself dictate survival.

page.mentor_intro: For suspected common bile duct stones, diagnostic guidelines have limited specificity and cannot reliably select patients for upfront ERCP. EUS before ERCP can spare about half of patients with bilirubin above 4 mg/dL and dilated duct a diagnostic ERCP, and EAES provides a rapid guideline on CBD stone management.

teaching_points.claim: The EAES rapid guideline updates management of common bile duct stones with network meta-analysis and GRADE.
Existing diagnostic guidelines for choledocholithiasis in acute biliary presentations have limited specificity for high-risk CBD stones and cannot reliably select patients for upfront ERCP.
Using endoscopic ultrasound to confirm CBD stones before ERCP can help almost half of patients with bilirubin above 4 mg/dL and a dilated CBD avoid diagnostic ERCP.
A surgery-first paediatric choledocholithiasis guideline was safe, feasible and effective using structured validated criteria.
A clinical practice guideline covers acute and chronic pancreatitis, with long-term care for uncomplicated disease with primary care and gastroenterology.
Predictors of post-ERCP pancreatitis were pooled to support risk prediction, informed consent and prevention.

A meta-analysis of 11 randomised trials found that NSAIDs control biliary colic pain with the same efficacy as opioids (RR 1.05), and significantly reduce complications compared with placebo (RR 0.53).

Natural history studies confirm that asymptomatic gallstones have a low annual risk of becoming symptomatic (1% to 2% per year), meaning prophylactic cholecystectomy is not indicated for uncomplicated asymptomatic cholelithiasis in the general population.

uncertainties: Pre-test risk stratification of CBD stones.

standard_knowledge.claim: Transabdominal ultrasound exhibits >95% sensitivity and specificity for detecting cholelithiasis, demonstrating mobile, echogenic foci with posterior acoustic shadowing within the gallbladder lumen.

Persistent right upper quadrant pain exceeding 6 hours accompanied by low-grade fever, leukocytosis, and a sonographic Murphy sign indicates transition from uncomplicated colic to acute calculous cholecystitis, mandating index-admission cholecystectomy.

page.standard_overview: Cholelithiasis is common in adult populations, with 10% to 20% developing symptoms over their lifetime. Uncomplicated biliary colic occurs when a gallstone transiently impacts the gallbladder neck or cystic duct during postprandial gallbladder contraction, producing episodic, severe right upper quadrant or epigastric pain that plateaus and resolves within 1 to 6 hours. The absence of systemic inflammation (fever, leukocytosis) and persistent peritoneal tenderness differentiates uncomplicated colic from acute cholecystitis. Transabdominal ultrasound is the first-line imaging test for gallstones, but biliary colic remains a clinical diagnosis and ultrasound alone does not prove that gallstones are the source of pain. NSAIDs are first-choice analgesics for biliary colic and have similar analgesic efficacy to opioids while reducing overall severe complications; the evidence does not specifically establish a reduction in progression to acute cholecystitis. Elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy is the definitive treatment for recurrent symptomatic biliary colic in patients who are suitable surgical candidates.

topic: Cholera and Vibrio infections: oral rehydration, doxycycline, epidemic control, vaccination

page.mentor_intro: Oral killed cholera vaccines give high-certainty protection with about 40% vaccine efficacy at two years. Paediatric diarrhoea guidance restricts antibiotics to dysentery-like symptoms, suspected cholera with severe dehydration or comorbidities, and antimicrobial resistance, including tetracycline, is rising in V. cholerae.

teaching_points.claim: A Chinese paediatric diarrhoea guideline recommends zinc for children over 6 months in deficient regions and restricts antibiotics to dysenteric symptoms, suspected cholera with severe dehydration, or comorbidities.
Oral killed cholera vaccines reduce cholera, with overall vaccine efficacy about 40% at both one- and two-year follow-up in a trial of 204,700 participants (high-certainty evidence).
Antimicrobial resistance is rising in V. cholerae, especially in low-income and endemic areas, so surveillance and appropriate susceptibility testing are crucial.
Tetracycline resistance among clinical V. cholerae isolates requires monitoring when choosing treatment.
Ciprofloxacin, azithromycin and other agents showed the best effectiveness against V. cholerae isolates in a resistance meta-analysis.
Non-cholera Vibrio infections carry a high burden in South Asia, with antibiotic-resistant and ESBL strains reported.

WHO guidelines mandate the use of reduced-osmolarity Oral Rehydration Solution (245 mOsm/L, containing 75 mmol/L sodium and 75 mmol/L glucose), which successfully rehydrates over 80-90% of cholera patients without intravenous therapy.

A large randomized cluster trial demonstrated that a single dose of oral inactivated whole-cell cholera vaccine provides significant protective efficacy (estimated 40-60%) in high-transmission endemic and epidemic settings.

uncertainties: Emerging resistance patterns.
case_hooks: Patient with profuse watery stool in an outbreak area.

standard_knowledge.claim: The primary cause of mortality in cholera is catastrophic hypovolemic shock and severe metabolic acidosis resulting from cholera toxin-induced hypersecretion of isotonic fluid across small bowel enterocytes.

In patients with severe dehydration, a single oral dose of doxycycline (300 mg in adults) or azithromycin (1 g in adults/children/pregnancy) significantly reduces diarrheal duration, total stool volume by 50%, and pathogen transmission.

page.standard_overview: Cholera is a virulent, water-borne epidemic diarrheal illness caused by toxigenic strains of Vibrio cholerae serogroups O1 and O139. Pathogenesis is driven by cholera enterotoxin, which activates intestinal mucosal adenylyl cyclase, leading to massive, unmitigated cyclic AMP-mediated chloride secretion and secretory diarrhea ('rice-water stools') that can exceed 1 liter per hour, precipitating lethal hypovolemic shock within hours. The cornerstone of case fatality reduction (<1%) is rapid, aggressive rehydration tailored to WHO dehydration protocols (Plans A, B, and C). The standard WHO reduced-osmolarity Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS, 245 mOsm/L) effectively treats mild-to-moderate dehydration, while severe dehydration mandates immediate intravenous Ringer's lactate. In appropriate patients with suspected or confirmed cholera, single-dose doxycycline or azithromycin can be used as an adjunct to rehydration, guided by local antimicrobial susceptibility; oral cholera vaccination is an effective preventive and outbreak-control measure.

page.mentor_intro: Retrieved evidence is mainly paediatric: functional abdominal pain disorders affect over 1 in 9 children, with CBT and hypnotherapy the best-supported psychosocial treatments and major evidence gaps for drug treatment. Adult chronic abdominal pain guidance is not covered.

teaching_points.claim: ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN guidelines for IBS and functional abdominal pain identified major evidence gaps and incentivise large paediatric trials.
A multidisciplinary expert consensus guides primary care providers in diagnosing and managing paediatric functional abdominal pain disorders.
Medical cannabis recommendations place it as third- or fourth-line therapy in chronic noncancer pain after detailed discussion of benefits and harms.
Video capsule endoscopy is a complementary test for GI bleeding, Crohn's or coeliac disease with negative or inconclusive prior studies.
Functional abdominal pain disorders affect over 1 in 9 children worldwide, more in girls and those with psychological stressors.
CBT and hypnotherapy may be considered for childhood functional abdominal pain disorders.
A probiotics meta-analysis in children with functional abdominal pain disorders found similar adverse event withdrawals between probiotic and placebo.
Vitamin D supplementation may help IBS with potential efficacy and good safety, pending further trials.

The ACG clinical guidelines endorse a positive diagnostic approach using Rome criteria alongside basic non-invasive tests (complete blood count, CRP/fecal calprotectin, celiac serology) rather than a strategy of exhaustive exclusion in patients lacking alarm features.

The Rome IV criteria establish a symptom-based positive diagnostic framework for disorders of gut-brain interaction, defining IBS as recurrent abdominal pain at least 1 day per week associated with defecation or change in stool frequency or form.

uncertainties: Drug treatments for paediatric functional pain lack trials.
case_hooks: Child with recurrent abdominal pain and normal examination.

standard_knowledge.claim: Central gut-brain neuromodulators, particularly tricyclic antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline 10-25 mg nocte), demonstrate significant efficacy in down-regulating visceral hypersensitivity and reducing pain severity in chronic abdominal pain.

The presence of red flag alarm features—nocturnal diarrhea, progressive dysphagia, hematochezia, unexplained anemia, or palpable abdominal mass—mandates urgent endoscopic and cross-sectional radiological investigations to exclude organic disease.

page.standard_overview: Chronic abdominal pain is a common, complex presentation that requires consideration of both organic disease and disorders of gut-brain interaction such as irritable bowel syndrome. Diagnostic evaluation should assess for alarm features, including gastrointestinal bleeding, unintended weight loss and a family history of colorectal cancer, with age and the full clinical context guiding the extent of investigation. In the absence of alarm signs, positive symptom-based diagnostic frameworks (Rome IV criteria) establish a diagnosis of IBS without exhaustive, invasive negative workups. Therapeutic management is individualized to the diagnosis and may include a limited low-FODMAP diet trial and gut-directed psychotherapy or other behavioral interventions, with drug therapy selected according to the patient's symptoms.

page.mentor_intro: Retrieved evidence spans organs. In kidney transplant, donor-derived cell-free DNA is a valuable marker for antibody-mediated rejection though less accurate for acute rejection, and imlifidase enables transplantation in highly sensitised patients. Antibody-mediated rejection is a critical unmet treatment need across heart and lung allografts.

teaching_points.claim: A risk-adapted approach to HLA delisting and imlifidase-enabled deceased-donor kidney transplantation addresses highly sensitised patients after kidney-preserving pathways are exhausted.
A JACC position statement highlights contemporary diagnosis and therapy of antibody-mediated rejection after heart transplantation, including complement-mediated injury and cytokine pathways.
The ISHLT scientific statement on pulmonary antibody-mediated rejection stresses better treatments as a critical unmet need and proposes a more precise definition.
An ISHLT consensus conference prepared a platform for further studies of antibodies and AMR in transplant patients.
A clinical consensus statement on heart transplantation covers cardiac allograft vasculopathy, infections and malignancies.
AASLD/AST guidance on liver transplant graft-related complications highlights the need to optimise management including recurrence prevention of alcohol-associated and metabolic liver disease.
Plasma donor-derived cell-free DNA accuracy for acute rejection in kidney allografts is limited by heterogeneity, but it is a valuable biomarker for antibody-mediated rejection.
At 7 years in the BENEFIT trial, belatacept-based immunosuppression was associated with a 43% reduction in the risk of death or graft loss compared with cyclosporine (hazard ratio 0.57).

Serial protocol biopsy studies demonstrate that early subclinical tubulitis and microvascular injury progress predictably to striped interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (IFTA) by 1 to 2 years post-transplantation.

uncertainties: Treatment of antibody-mediated rejection.

standard_knowledge.claim: The Banff 2017 classification defines chronic active antibody-mediated rejection (cABMR) by morphologic evidence of chronic tissue injury (transplant glomerulopathy), microvascular inflammation, and serologic or immunohistochemical evidence of donor-specific antibodies (DSA) or C4d staining.
Antibody-mediated rejection and non-adherence to immunosuppression are the predominant causes of late kidney transplant loss, well ahead of classic chronic calcineurin inhibitor toxicity.

page.standard_overview: Chronic kidney allograft dysfunction is a major cause of late graft loss and may present with declining eGFR, proteinuria and worsening hypertension; interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy are common histologic findings but are not specific to a single cause. Chronic active antibody-mediated rejection is an important cause of chronic kidney allograft dysfunction and is assessed using Banff criteria that integrate histologic injury with immunologic evidence such as donor-specific antibodies; microvascular inflammation and transplant glomerulopathy are characteristic findings. Secondary contributors include calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) nephrotoxicity, recurrent or de novo glomerulonephritis, and polyomavirus (BK) nephropathy. Management begins with evaluation of the cause of dysfunction, often including an indication biopsy, followed by individualized optimization of immunosuppression and treatment of reversible contributors; no single regimen is effective for every cause.

topic: Chronic aortic regurgitation: surveillance intervals and surgical timing

page.mentor_intro: In chronic aortic regurgitation, vena contracta width and LV volumes reliably identify significant disease, while CMR and global longitudinal strain add prognostic information in asymptomatic patients. Reviews suggest surgery timed earlier than current guidelines may give survival benefit, but randomised trials are lacking.

teaching_points.claim: A simplified echo approach using vena contracta width and LV volumes can reliably identify significant AR when compared with CMR.
Myocardial remodelling assessment beyond volumes and function may identify irreversible myocardial injury earlier.
Studies of AR, AS and mixed disease found long-term survival benefit from surgery earlier than current guideline timing, but RCTs are required.
Global longitudinal strain is a prognostic biomarker in asymptomatic moderate-to-severe AR with preserved LVEF and may help timing of surgery, though thresholds need validation.
Multi-parameter CMR predicts aortic valve surgery as an endpoint in chronic AR.

The 2021 ESC/EACTS guidelines recommend aortic valve surgery for severe chronic AR in all symptomatic patients, and in asymptomatic patients who develop resting LVEF <=50% or resting LVESD >50 mm (>25 mm/m²).

The 2020 ACC/AHA guidelines establish that asymptomatic severe AR patients with normal LV systolic function should undergo clinical and echocardiographic re-evaluation every 6 to 12 months, and sooner if LV dilation approaches surgical thresholds.

Quantitative echocardiographic criteria for severe chronic aortic regurgitation include a regurgitant volume >=60 mL/beat, an effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) >=0.30 cm², and a vena contracta width >6 mm.

uncertainties: Optimal timing of surgery in asymptomatic patients.
case_hooks: Asymptomatic young adult with severe AR and LVEF 55%.

standard_knowledge.claim: Landmark prospective surgical cohorts from the NIH demonstrated that delaying aortic valve replacement until left ventricular ejection fraction falls below 50% or LVESD exceeds 50-55 mm leads to incomplete post-operative LV recovery and excess late mortality.

page.standard_overview: Chronic aortic regurgitation imposes left ventricular volume and pressure overload, leading to eccentric hypertrophy and chamber dilation that can preserve forward stroke volume during a prolonged compensated phase. Patients with severe aortic regurgitation can remain asymptomatic while subclinical myocardial injury develops; CMR-detected fibrosis is associated with adverse outcomes and may mark irreversible damage, but its role in routine risk stratification remains under evaluation. The 2021 ESC/EACTS guideline recommends surgery for symptomatic severe AR and for asymptomatic severe AR with resting LVEF <=50%, LVESD >50 mm or indexed LVESD >25 mm/m²; the 2020 ACC/AHA guideline uses an LVEF threshold of <=55% for asymptomatic severe AR with left ventricular systolic dysfunction. For asymptomatic severe aortic regurgitation, clinical review and surveillance echocardiography are generally performed every 6-12 months, with the interval individualized to severity, ventricular size and function, and rate of change; less frequent imaging is appropriate for milder stable disease.

page.mentor_intro: Retrieved evidence addresses risk factors rather than treatment: rhinovirus bronchiolitis is more strongly associated than RSV with later recurrent wheeze and asthma, and particulate pollution and Mycoplasma infection are associated with childhood asthma. Mediterranean diet shows a low-certainty inverse association.

teaching_points.claim: Rhinovirus-induced bronchiolitis was more strongly associated than RSV bronchiolitis with recurrent wheeze and childhood asthma.
Childhood asthma prevalence is highest in Oceania and lower in Eurasia, with modifiable risk factors identified.
Exposure to particulate matter is associated with developing asthma and wheeze in children, supporting measures to reduce particle pollution.
Black and organic carbon and ammonium in PM2.5 mainly contributed to increased childhood asthma risk.
Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection is positively associated with childhood asthma, though causal mechanisms are unclear.
Mediterranean diet adherence shows a trend to inverse association with childhood asthma with low certainty.

The GINA strategy establishes that SABA-only treatment without concurrent inhaled corticosteroid is no longer recommended for adults and adolescents, as it fails to protect against severe exacerbations and down-regulates beta-receptors.

In the randomised double-blind SYGMA 2 trial, as-needed budesonide-formoterol was non-inferior to twice-daily maintenance budesonide for preventing severe exacerbations, with roughly 80% lower inhaled glucocorticoid exposure.

The NOVEL START open-label randomized trial demonstrated that as-needed budesonide-formoterol was significantly superior to as-needed SABA alone in preventing severe asthma exacerbations (RR 0.49) in patients with mild asthma.

uncertainties: Causality of infection and diet associations.
case_hooks: Toddler with recurrent wheeze after rhinovirus bronchiolitis.

standard_knowledge.claim: Single maintenance and reliever therapy (SMART/MART) with low-dose ICS-formoterol across Steps 3-5 provides immediate symptom relief while dynamically titrating anti-inflammatory therapy during early worsening, reducing exacerbation hospitalizations by over 30%.

page.standard_overview: Asthma is a heterogeneous chronic inflammatory disease of the airways, with recurrent wheeze, breathlessness, chest tightness and cough and variable expiratory airflow limitation. The paradigm of asthma management underwent a fundamental shift in the Global Initiative for Asthma (GINA) strategy by eliminating short-acting beta2-agonist (SABA) monotherapy due to its association with increased exacerbation and death risks. GINA Track 1 uses low-dose ICS-formoterol as the preferred reliever across Steps 1-5; in Steps 1-2 it is taken only as needed, while in Steps 3-5 it is used as maintenance-and-reliever therapy (SMART/MART), providing anti-inflammatory treatment with each reliever dose and reducing severe exacerbations.

topic: Chronic coronary syndrome: stable angina assessment and revascularisation decisions

page.mentor_intro: The 2024 ESC chronic coronary syndrome guideline sets antithrombotic regimens, and a systematic review of CCS guidelines calls for higher-quality evidence-based guidance. A meta-analysis found revascularisation improved outcomes over optimal medical treatment, with greater benefit at longer follow-up.

teaching_points.claim: A review of the 2024 ESC guidelines covers oral antithrombotic regimens in chronic coronary syndrome and compares them with a European expert consensus.
A systematic review of CCS clinical practice guidelines calls for stronger multidisciplinary efforts toward higher-quality evidence-based guidelines.
Revascularisation was associated with better clinical outcomes than optimal medical treatment in CCS, with larger benefit at longer follow-up and a role for personalised choice.
Atherogenic index of plasma is linked to CAD risk, severity and prognosis, with optimal cut-offs unclear.
Triglyceride-glucose index is associated with in-stent restenosis after PCI.

The 2019 ESC guidelines define specific anatomical indications where revascularization confers a proven survival benefit: significant left main coronary stenosis (>=50%), proximal LAD disease, multivessel CAD with reduced LVEF (<=35%), or extensive ischemia (>10% of LV).

In the landmark ISCHEMIA trial of 5,179 patients with stable coronary disease and moderate-to-severe ischemia, an initial invasive strategy (angiography and revascularization) did not reduce ischemic cardiovascular events or all-cause mortality compared to optimal medical therapy.

In the ISCHEMIA trial quality-of-life analysis, revascularization resulted in significant, durable improvements in angina-related health status and symptom frequency in patients who had daily or weekly angina at baseline.

The landmark COURAGE trial previously demonstrated that percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) added to optimal medical therapy did not reduce the risk of death, myocardial infarction, or other major cardiovascular events in patients with stable angina.

uncertainties: Benefit of revascularisation relative to modern medical therapy.
case_hooks: Stable angina on beta-blocker with positive stress test.

page.standard_overview: Chronic coronary syndromes (CCS) describe the long-term, non-acute stages of coronary artery disease. The 2024 ESC guidelines recommend a structured risk factor-weighted clinical likelihood (RF-CL) estimate of obstructive CAD as the first step after history taking, to triage testing and to identify very-low-likelihood patients in whom further testing can be deferred. Coronary CT angiography is used to rule out obstructive CAD in patients with low to intermediate pre-test probability. The decision to revascularize was redefined by the landmark ISCHEMIA trial: in patients with stable coronary disease and moderate-to-severe ischemia, an initial routine invasive strategy (PCI or CABG) did NOT reduce major adverse cardiovascular events (death or MI) compared to optimal medical therapy (OMT), though it provided significant angina relief. Revascularisation improves prognosis mainly in left main disease, multivessel disease, proximal LAD involvement and severe LV systolic dysfunction. In other patients it mainly relieves angina and improves quality of life, and it is considered when symptoms persist despite guideline-directed medical therapy.

topic: chronic cough evaluation and empiric therapy

page.mentor_intro: CHEST guidelines treat chronic cough by cause and population: extraesophageal reflux symptoms improving on a PPI should not be taken as proof of GERD, children should not receive GERD treatment without GERD features, and ILD-associated cough has limited evidence.

teaching_points.claim: AGA best practice advice says symptom improvement on PPI in extraesophageal reflux may arise from non-acid mechanisms and does not confirm GERD.
In children with chronic cough, GERD treatment should not be used without clinical features of GERD, and paediatric GERD guidelines should guide investigation.
The CHEST paediatric chronic cough guideline now has high-quality evidence for some management aspects, with further primary care studies needed.
Aetiologies of chronic cough in children differ from adults and depend on age and setting.
The CHEST guideline on cough due to asthma and non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis addresses non-invasive airway inflammation measurement and treatment.
Evidence for managing chronic cough in interstitial lung disease is limited.
The Chinese national cough guideline covers evaluation, diagnosis, and empirical and symptomatic treatment of chronic cough.

The European Respiratory Society (ERS) guideline recommends a trial of inhaled corticosteroids for suspected cough-variant asthma or eosinophilic bronchitis, and proton pump inhibitors or prokinetics when reflux symptoms accompany chronic cough.

The CHEST guideline diagnostic protocol establishes that in patients with chronic cough and a normal chest radiograph, the initial step is discontinuing ACE inhibitors, followed by sequential evaluation and treatment of UACS, asthma/NAEB, and GERD.
In the COUGH-1 and COUGH-2 trials, the P2X3 antagonist gefapixant 45 mg twice daily reduced 24-hour cough frequency by about 15 to 18% versus placebo in refractory or unexplained chronic cough.

uncertainties: Evidence for ILD cough therapy is limited.
case_hooks: Non-smoker with chronic dry cough and normal chest radiograph.

page.standard_overview: Chronic cough in adults—defined as a cough lasting longer than 8 weeks—is one of the most common reasons for primary and secondary care consultations. Following normal chest radiography and cessation of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, most cases of chronic cough are driven by the classic 'pathogenic triad': upper airway cough syndrome (UACS, formerly post-nasal drip), cough-variant asthma (CVA) or non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis (NAEB), and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), including non-acid reflux. Initial assessment includes chest radiography and spirometry, with empiric and targeted treatment for the most common causes (upper airway cough syndrome, asthma, nonasthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis, reflux); bronchoscopy and nasendoscopy follow if initial tests are unremarkable. ERS guidelines describe treatable traits such as cough variant asthma/eosinophilic bronchitis and non-acid reflux. For refractory, unexplained chronic cough (cough hypersensitivity syndrome), novel P2X3 purinergic receptor antagonists provide targeted neuronal suppression.

page.standard_overview: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection affects over 250 million individuals worldwide, posing substantial risks of cirrhosis, liver failure, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). International clinical guidelines from EASL and AASLD recommend long-term treatment with oral nucleos(t)ide analogues (NUCs) possessing a high genetic barrier to resistance: entecavir (ETV), tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF), and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF). Treatment is typically indicated when HBV DNA exceeds 2,000 IU/mL with elevated ALT and/or at least moderate necroinflammation or fibrosis, and in every patient with cirrhosis who has detectable HBV DNA regardless of ALT. Long-term viral suppression limits disease progression, can promote fibrosis regression and reduces but does not eliminate HCC risk; HBsAg clearance is the functional-cure endpoint, while ongoing risk-based clinical and HCC monitoring remains necessary.

page.standard_overview: CIDP is a chronic immune-mediated neuropathy; the 2021 EAN/PNS guideline distinguishes typical CIDP from variants (multifocal, focal, distal, motor, sensory). EAN/PNS guidelines strongly recommend IVIG or corticosteroids as initial CIDP treatment and strongly recommend plasma exchange when IVIG and corticosteroids are ineffective; plasma exchange is an effective therapy but not an equal first-line recommendation. For initial treatment of typical CIDP and its variants, IVIg or corticosteroids are strongly recommended; plasma exchange is recommended if both are ineffective; IVIg is considered first-line in motor CIDP. Maintenance regimens may use subcutaneous immunoglobulin, which produces stable IgG levels and can reduce end-of-dose wear-off fluctuations associated with intermittent IVIG.

page.standard_overview: CIDP diagnosis rests on clinical and electrodiagnostic features. The 2021 EAN/PNS guideline gives good practice points for supportive criteria and investigations. The 2021 EAN/PNS guideline reduced diagnostic certainty from three levels (definite, probable, possible) to two (CIDP and possible CIDP), because the diagnostic accuracy of the probable and definite criteria did not differ significantly. The electrodiagnostic criteria were revised in 2021. In a cohort of 339 patients and 339 controls, sensitivity was 94% for possible CIDP (2010 guideline: 92%) and 83% for CIDP (2010 probable/definite: 91%), with specificities of 66% and 86% (2010: 67% and 78%). Unilateral nerve conduction studies would miss 77 possible CIDP diagnoses. A critical conceptual advance is distinguishing typical CIDP and clinical variants (multifocal [MADSAM], focal, pure sensory, distal [DADS]) from autoantibody-mediated 'autoimmune nodopathies' (targeting contactin-1, Caspr1, or neurofascin-155), which show poor response to IVIG but often respond to B-cell depletion with rituximab.

page.standard_overview: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors have revolutionized the therapeutic landscape of chronic kidney disease, emerging as foundational, disease-modifying nephroprotective and cardioprotective agents. Beyond lowering glucose, SGLT2 inhibitors act on glomerular haemodynamics by restoring tubuloglomerular feedback and lowering intraglomerular pressure. CREDENCE, DAPA-CKD and EMPA-KIDNEY established kidney protection with SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with and without type 2 diabetes, across a broad range of eGFR and albuminuria. SGLT2 inhibitors reduce albuminuria, slow eGFR decline and lower the risk of progression to end-stage kidney disease.

page.standard_overview: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is the most prevalent adult leukemia in Western countries, defined by the clonal proliferation and accumulation of mature, incompetent B lymphocytes (>=5 x 10^9/L) co-expressing CD5, CD19, and CD23 with weak surface immunoglobulin and CD20 expression. Clinical staging uses the Rai and Binet systems, which correlate with survival in advanced disease but do not separate progressive from stable early disease. Treatment is started when iwCLL criteria for active disease are met; asymptomatic early-stage disease is observed (watch and wait). Indications for active treatment ('active disease') include progressive bone marrow failure, massive or progressive splenomegaly/lymphadenopathy, rapid lymphocyte doubling time (<6 months), or constitutional B symptoms. First-line options are continuous BTK inhibition or fixed-duration venetoclax regimens (venetoclax-obinutuzumab, venetoclax-ibrutinib). In a 909-patient phase 3 trial, 3-year progression-free survival was 81.1% (venetoclax-obinutuzumab), 79.4% (venetoclax-ibrutinib) and 81.0% (ibrutinib), and each fixed-duration arm met non-inferiority.

The iwCLL guidelines establish TP53 disruption (del(17p) or TP53 mutation) as an absolute contraindication to FCR or any chemoimmunotherapy due to primary chemoresistance, mandating targeted novel oral therapies.

In the randomized phase 3 CLL8 trial, adding rituximab to fludarabine and cyclophosphamide (FCR) significantly improved overall response rate (90% vs 80%), progression-free survival (median 51.8 vs 32.8 months), and 3-year overall survival (87% vs 83%).

Long-term follow-up of the CLL8 trial demonstrated a durable survival plateau in patients with mutated IGHV treated with FCR, with over 50% remaining disease-free at 10 years without subsequent therapy, consistent with operational cure.

In the E1912 trial in untreated fit CLL patients aged 70 or younger, ibrutinib plus rituximab improved progression-free survival (HR about 0.35) and overall survival (HR about 0.17) compared with FCR.

page.standard_overview: The chemoimmunotherapy regimen comprising fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, and rituximab (FCR) represents a historic benchmark in the treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). The pivotal German CLL Study Group CLL8 trial established that FCR significantly prolonged progression-free and overall survival compared to FC chemotherapy alone. In the CLL8 trial (817 patients), FCR gave median progression-free survival of 56.8 versus 32.9 months with FC (HR 0.59) and longer overall survival (HR 0.68). In patients with mutated IGHV, FCR improved PFS (HR 0.47), and the benefit held across cytogenetic subgroups other than del(17p). The benefit of FCR did not extend to del(17p), and how to treat IGHV-unmutated disease remains an open question. Targeted BTK or BCL-2 inhibitor regimens are preferred for TP53-disrupted disease.

page.standard_overview: The front-line and relapsed treatment paradigm for chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is anchored by targeted oral therapies that bypass TP53 aberrations and standard chemoresistance pathways. Clinicians choose between continuous BTK inhibition and fixed-duration venetoclax regimens combined with obinutuzumab or ibrutinib; a randomised comparison found non-inferior 3-year progression-free survival with the fixed-duration regimens. Head-to-head randomized trials (ALPINE and ELEVATE-RR) showed that second-generation BTK inhibitors have at least equivalent efficacy to ibrutinib (zanubrutinib was superior in ALPINE) and lower rates of atrial fibrillation. After fixed-duration treatment, peripheral-blood minimal residual disease was undetectable in 73.3% of patients on venetoclax-obinutuzumab and 47.2% on venetoclax-ibrutinib.

page.standard_overview: Chronic myeloid leukaemia is a haematopoietic stem cell malignancy characterised by the Philadelphia chromosome, a reciprocal t(9;22) translocation that produces the BCR::ABL1 fusion protein, the main driver of the disease. Unregulated tyrosine kinase signaling drives granulocytic proliferation, splenomegaly, and a predictable progression from chronic phase to accelerated and fatal blast phase. Management follows European LeukemiaNet recommendations (updates in 2006, 2009, 2013, 2020 and 2025), which moved from cytogenetic to molecular monitoring and introduced treatment-free remission as a goal. The 3-, 6- and 12-month RT-qPCR time points on the International Scale are in the ELN full text, not in the abstract. Early molecular milestones of BCR-ABL1 at most 10% at 3 months, 1% at 6 months and 0.1% (major molecular response) at 12 months identify favorable response; treatment-free remission requires a subsequent sustained deep molecular response and careful molecular monitoring.

page.standard_overview: First-line selection of tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy in chronic-phase CML balances potency against distinct comorbidity-specific toxicity profiles. Second-generation TKIs (dasatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib) induce significantly faster, deeper molecular remissions than first-generation imatinib, making them advantageous when rapid disease control or future treatment-free remission is prioritized. However, 10-year overall survival remains virtually identical across all agents due to effective sequential salvage. Patient selection is largely driven by cardiovascular, pulmonary, and metabolic comorbidities: nilotinib is associated with arterial occlusive disease and hyperglycemia, dasatinib carries risks of pleural effusions and pulmonary arterial hypertension, bosutinib commonly causes gastrointestinal toxicity, and imatinib causes fluid retention.

In the original phase 3 IRIS trial, imatinib induced complete hematologic response in 95% and complete cytogenetic response in 76% of patients at 18 months, dramatically outperforming interferon alfa plus cytarabine.

The 10-year follow-up of the IRIS trial confirmed long-term overall survival of 83.3%, with a cumulative complete cytogenetic response rate of 82.8% and no new or late safety concerns, establishing imatinib as an exceptionally durable therapy.

The BCR-ABL1 gatekeeper mutation T315I ('threonine-to-isoleucine substitution at position 315') prevents binding of imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib through steric clash, but remains sensitive to the third-generation inhibitor ponatinib (PACE trial).

Asciminib acts as a Specifically Targeting the ABL Myristoyl Pocket (STAMP) allosteric inhibitor, demonstrating superior major molecular response rates (25.5% vs 13.2%) and lower toxicity compared to bosutinib in the phase 3 ASCEMBL trial.

page.standard_overview: Imatinib mesylate, a competitive 2-phenylaminopyrimidine inhibitor of the ATP-binding site of the BCR-ABL1 tyrosine kinase, represents the foundational breakthrough of modern precision oncology. In the pivotal IRIS trial, imatinib dismantled the dogma that CML required toxic allogeneic bone marrow transplantation, achieving unprecedented durable cytogenetic and molecular responses. Ten-year follow-up demonstrated an estimated overall survival of 83.3%, with the vast majority of deaths unrelated to CML. However, up to 20-30% of patients develop primary resistance or secondary loss of response, predominantly mediated by point mutations in the BCR-ABL1 kinase domain. The gatekeeper T315I mutation confers absolute resistance to imatinib and all second-generation TKIs, requiring third-generation ponatinib or the STAMP allosteric inhibitor asciminib.

CMML is diagnosed by persistent peripheral blood monocytosis (1.0 x 10^9/L or more in WHO 2016; 0.5 x 10^9/L or more with dysplasia or clonal evidence in WHO 2022) with monocytes at least 10% of leukocytes, fewer than 20% blasts, and no BCR::ABL1.

page.standard_overview: Chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) is a clonal hematopoietic stem cell neoplasm categorized as an overlap myelodysplastic/myeloproliferative neoplasm (MDS/MPN). CMML diagnosis requires persistent peripheral blood monocytosis of at least 1 x 10^9/L with monocytes at least 10% of the white cell count (WHO 2016), together with exclusion of other myeloid neoplasms; no clinical, pathological or molecular finding is specific, so it remains a diagnosis of exclusion. CMML is classified by blast and promonocyte count into CMML-0, 1 and 2, and by white cell count into dysplastic (WBC under 13 x 10^9/L) and proliferative (WBC 13 x 10^9/L or more) forms. Proliferative CMML has a more aggressive course with higher rates of transformation to AML. CPSS-Mol integrates clinical, cytogenetic and selected somatic-mutation data, including adverse ASXL1 status, to refine prognosis and inform decisions such as allogeneic transplantation; TET2 and SRSF2 are common CMML mutations but are not the defining adverse molecular components of CPSS-Mol.

page.standard_overview: Chronic neutrophilic leukemia (CNL) is an exceptionally rare BCR-ABL1-negative myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) characterized by sustained, mature neutrophilic leukocytosis without dysgranulopoiesis. CNL is a rare myeloproliferative neoplasm with peripheral blood neutrophilia, marrow granulocyte hyperplasia, hepatosplenomegaly and activating CSF3R mutations. The WHO numeric thresholds (WBC at least 25 x 10^9/L, at least 80% neutrophils, under 10% immature forms) are not in the abstracts and are flagged. The genomic landmark was the discovery of oncogenic colony-stimulating factor 3 receptor (CSF3R) mutations—predominantly the membrane-proximal T618I missense mutation—present in >80% of bona fide CNL cases, which drives ligand-independent dimerization and constitutive downstream JAK-STAT pathway activation. CNL has an adverse prognosis with a risk of transformation to acute myeloid leukemia; ruxolitinib has shown clinical activity in appropriate CSF3R-mutated disease, including improvement in splenomegaly and leukocytosis.

page.standard_overview: Chronic pancreatitis is a progressive, irreversible fibro-inflammatory disease of the pancreas characterized by repetitive episodes of parenchymal necrosis, ductal obstruction, and chronic inflammation leading to extensive acinar atrophy and dense interlobular fibrosis. Classified etiologically using the TIGAR-O system (Toxic-metabolic [alcohol, smoking], Idiopathic, Genetic [PRSS1, SPINK1, CFTR], Autoimmune, Recurrent acute pancreatitis, and Obstructive), smoking and heavy alcohol consumption act synergistically as predominant Western drivers. Diagnosis relies on cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI/MRCP demonstrating parenchymal atrophy, coarse intraductal calcifications, and main pancreatic duct irregular dilation). Advanced chronic pancreatitis causes exocrine insufficiency (malabsorption with steatorrhoea, detected by faecal elastase) and endocrine failure (pancreatogenic type 3c diabetes, with unstable glycaemia).

page.standard_overview: The management of chronic pancreatitis requires simultaneously addressing intractable abdominal pain and pancreatic exocrine insufficiency (PEI). Pain pathophysiology is multifactorial, arising from intraductal hypertension, parenchymal compartment syndrome, and central neuropathic sensitization. Clinical guidelines advocate a stepwise approach: total cessation of alcohol and tobacco, non-opioid analgesia with adjunctive neuromodulators (pregabalin/gabapentin), and endoscopic or surgical decompression. In selected patients with painful obstructive chronic pancreatitis and a dilated pancreatic duct, a randomized trial found surgical drainage provided superior and more durable pain relief than endoscopic drainage; the appropriate operation depends on anatomy and clinical context. For PEI, adequately dosed enteric-coated PERT taken with meals improves fat absorption and nutritional status; the dose should be titrated to response, while bone health requires nutritional monitoring and management, and a survival benefit has not been established by the cited evidence.

page.standard_overview: Chronic spontaneous urticaria is defined by recurrent itchy wheals, angioedema, or both for >=6 weeks without an identifiable external trigger; individual wheals are transient, usually resolving within 24 hours, even though the disease persists or recurs. Chronic spontaneous urticaria is a mast cell-driven disease with two main endotypes: autoallergic (type I, IgE) and autoimmune (type IIb, functional IgG autoantibodies against FcεRIα or IgE). The international EAACI/GA2LEN/EuroGuiDerm/APAAACI guideline establishes a stepped algorithm: Step 1 initiates standard-dose second-generation H1-antihistamines; Step 2 escalates to high-dose antihistamines (up to four-fold approved doses); Step 3 introduces omalizumab (monoclonal antibody targeting the C-epsilon-3 domain of human IgE, 300 mg subcutaneous every 4 weeks). Pivotal phase 3 trials (ASTERIA I and II) showed that omalizumab significantly improved UAS7, itch severity, and quality of life versus placebo in antihistamine-refractory CSU, with a favourable safety profile.

page.standard_overview: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH, Group 4 PH) is a unique, potentially curable form of pulmonary hypertension characterized by organized, fibrotic thromboemboli persistently obstructing elastic pulmonary arteries, accompanied by a secondary microvasculopathy in non-obstructed vascular beds. The incidence of CTEPH after acute pulmonary embolism is uncertain. Ventilation-perfusion scintigraphy is the preferred imaging modality for detecting chronic thromboembolic obstruction. CTEPH is diagnosed with right heart catheterisation after effective anticoagulation, supported by echocardiography, V/Q scanning and pulmonary angiography. The haemodynamic thresholds (mean PAP above 20 mmHg, wedge pressure 15 mmHg or less, PVR 2 Wood units or more) are in the ESC/ERS guideline, not in the abstracts, and are flagged. All patients should be assessed by an expert CTEPH multidisciplinary team; PEA is the preferred potentially curative treatment for operable disease, while operability and treatment selection depend on individual assessment. For inoperable disease, balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) and riociguat provide proven clinical efficacy.

page.standard_overview: Chronic tophaceous gout represents the advanced, destructive phase of gout characterized by the chronic deposition of monosodium urate (MSU) crystal aggregates within cartilage, synovial membranes, tendons, and periarticular soft tissues. Tophi are chronic foreign-body granuloma-like structures of monosodium urate crystals surrounded by inflammatory cells and connective tissue, and are implicated in structural joint damage. Diagnosis is confirmed by demonstrating negatively birefringent needle-shaped MSU crystals on polarizing microscopy or via dual-energy CT (DECT) depicting volumetric urate deposits. Effective treatment of tophaceous gout requires long-term urate-lowering therapy, ideally to a serum urate below 5 mg/dL (300 umol/L). Newer urate-lowering options allow faster tophus regression in severe tophaceous gout. Stepwise-titrated allopurinol as first line and pegloticase for refractory disease are standard teaching; no abstract found for them (flagged).

page.standard_overview: Chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) affects up to 25% of adults, arising from ambulatory venous hypertension triggered by valvular incompetence, deep venous obstruction, and calf muscle pump failure. Classified internationally using the CEAP system (C0 [asymptomatic] to C6 [active venous leg ulcer]), severe CVI manifests as lipodermatosclerosis, atrophie blanche, hemosiderin hyperpigmentation, and chronic non-healing ulcerations over the medial malleolus. The cornerstone of conservative management is multi-layer graduated compression therapy (delivering 30-40 mmHg at the ankle). The landmark randomized EVRA trial revolutionized surgical practice by demonstrating that early endovenous ablation of superficial truncal venous reflux (radiofrequency or laser) within 2 weeks accelerates venous ulcer healing and significantly prolongs ulcer-free time.

standard_knowledge.claim: Management of acute variceal hemorrhage requires immediate vasoactive drug infusion (terlipressin, octreotide, or somatostatin), prophylactic ceftriaxone, restrictive blood transfusion (target Hb 70-80 g/L), and endoscopic band ligation within 12 hours.

Non-selective beta-blockers (propranolol, nadolol, carvedilol) reduce portal pressure by blocking beta-1 cardiac output and beta-2 splanchnic vasoconstriction, reducing the risk of first variceal hemorrhage by ~50%.

page.standard_overview: Portal hypertension is the primary hemodynamic consequence of cirrhosis, initiated by increased intrahepatic vascular resistance and aggravated by splanchnic arterial vasodilation and hyperdynamic systemic circulation. Defined by a hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) >5 mmHg, clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH, HVPG >=10 mmHg) drives major clinical decompensations, including gastroesophageal varices, ascites, and hepatic encephalopathy. Baveno VII supports liver stiffness >=25 kPa by transient elastography to rule in CSPH in appropriate patients with compensated advanced chronic liver disease, and liver stiffness <=20 kPa plus platelet count >=150 x 10^9/L to rule out high-risk varices in eligible patients, allowing endoscopy to be avoided when the applicable criteria are met. Primary prophylaxis of variceal bleeding centers on non-selective beta-blockers (NSBBs, particularly carvedilol due to intrinsic alpha-1 adrenergic antagonism lowering intrahepatic resistance) or endoscopic variceal band ligation (EVL).

topic: Cirrhosis ascites and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis

page.mentor_intro: Ascites guidelines manage cirrhotic ascites with attention to albumin use, infection and hepatorenal syndrome; terlipressin plus albumin treats HRS. TIPS prevents further decompensation and improves survival in selected cirrhosis with portal hypertension.

teaching_points.claim: Chest 2024: Recommendation 11: In patients with cirrhosis and spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, intravenous albumin is suggested to reduce mortality (Conditional Recommendation, Low Certainty of Evidence of Effect).

Guidelines on the management of ascites in cirrhosis use GRADE methodology and are intended to inform practising clinicians.
For hepatorenal syndrome, the Chinese ascites guideline recommends vasopressor terlipressin with albumin, and local microbiology guides anti-infection treatment.
The AGA update on AKI in cirrhosis advises that TIPS should not be used as specific treatment of HRS and addresses renal replacement therapy in selected circumstances.
Few evidence-based indications support routine albumin use, and guidelines give actionable recommendations on appropriate use.
A comparison found good concordance between European, American and British guidelines on ascites, SBP and HRS, recommending vasoactive drugs.
TIPS reduces further decompensation and increases survival compared with standard care in cirrhosis with portal hypertension-related complications.

The EASL clinical practice guidelines establish that diagnostic paracentesis must be performed in all cirrhotic patients admitted with ascites, defining SBP as an ascitic fluid neutrophil count >=250 cells/mm³ (>=0.25 x 10^9/L).

The AASLD guideline recommends indefinite secondary antimicrobial prophylaxis (ciprofloxacin, norfloxacin, or TMP-SMX) following an index episode of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis to prevent recurrence.

In a landmark randomized trial by Sort et al., intravenous albumin (1.5 g/kg on day 1, 1.0 g/kg on day 3) added to cefotaxime significantly reduced renal impairment (10% vs 33%) and in-hospital mortality (10% vs 29%) in cirrhotic patients with SBP.

page.standard_overview: Ascites is the most common decompensating complication of cirrhosis, portending a 50% mortality at 2 years in the absence of liver transplantation. Diagnostic abdominal paracentesis is mandatory for all patients presenting with new-onset or hospital-admitted ascites to calculate the Serum-Ascites Albumin Gradient (SAAG; >=1.1 g/dL indicates portal hypertension) and rule out spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP). SBP is defined by an ascitic fluid absolute polymorphonuclear (PMN) neutrophil count >=250 cells/mm³ (>=0.25 x 10^9/L), regardless of culture status. Prompt empiric antibiotics guided by acquisition and local resistance, commonly cefotaxime or ceftriaxone for community-acquired SBP, should be combined with intravenous albumin 1.5 g/kg at diagnosis and 1.0 g/kg on day 3 in appropriate patients. In a randomized trial, adding albumin to cefotaxime reduced renal impairment from 33% to 10% and in-hospital mortality from 29% to 10% in patients with SBP.

page.standard_overview: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and premature mortality in chronic kidney disease (CKD), with patients far more likely to die of a cardiovascular event than to progress to dialysis. Beyond traditional Framingham risk factors, CKD accelerates non-atherosclerotic vascular calcification, arterial stiffness, left ventricular hypertrophy, and sudden cardiac death driven by uremic toxins, chronic volume overload, sympathetic hyperactivation, and CKD-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD). The SHARP trial established that lowering LDL-cholesterol with simvastatin plus ezetimibe significantly reduces major atherosclerotic events in non-dialysis CKD. The 4D and AURORA trials did not show significant primary cardiovascular-outcome benefit from initiating statin therapy during maintenance dialysis, supporting guidelines that generally advise against starting statins in dialysis patients while not requiring withdrawal of therapy already established before dialysis.

The KDIGO 2017 CKD-MBD guideline update defines CKD-MBD as a systemic disorder manifested by laboratory abnormalities (calcium, phosphate, PTH, FGF-23, vitamin D), alterations in bone morphology and strength, and extra-skeletal vascular calcification.

standard_knowledge.claim: Renal osteodystrophy encompasses a histological continuum ranging from high-turnover bone disease (osteitis fibrosa cystica driven by severe secondary hyperparathyroidism) to low-turnover adynamic bone disease caused by excessive PTH suppression.

Calciphylaxis (calcific uremic arteriolopathy) is a catastrophic complication of advanced CKD characterized by medial calcification and intimal hyperplasia of small cutaneous arterioles, producing painful ischemic livedo reticularis, subcutaneous plaques, and necrotic ulcers.

page.standard_overview: Chronic Kidney Disease-Mineral and Bone Disorder (CKD-MBD) is a complex systemic syndrome initiated by progressive nephron loss that disrupts calcium, phosphate, vitamin D, and parathyroid hormone (PTH) homeostasis. Early in CKD, phosphate retention and reduced klotho signaling are accompanied by increased osteocyte-derived FGF-23, which suppresses renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase and lowers 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D; hypocalcemia is not an inevitable early consequence. These abnormalities contribute to secondary hyperparathyroidism and the CKD-MBD triad of biochemical disturbances, renal osteodystrophy ranging from high- to low-turnover bone disease, and vascular or soft-tissue calcification; calciphylaxis is an uncommon severe complication rather than an inevitable endpoint.

page.standard_overview: Medical management of CKD-MBD focuses on lowering serum phosphate toward the normal range, preventing hypercalcemia, and controlling secondary hyperparathyroidism without inducing adynamic bone disease. Dietary phosphate restriction is combined with oral phosphate binders taken with meals. Guidelines suggest restricting calcium-based phosphate binders, particularly with hypercalcemia, adynamic bone disease, or vascular calcification; non-calcium binders such as sevelamer or lanthanum avoid calcium loading, but agent selection is individualized. In dialysis patients, secondary hyperparathyroidism is managed using calcimimetics (cinacalcet or intravenous etelcalcetide), which allosterically activate the parathyroid calcium-sensing receptor to suppress PTH secretion without increasing serum calcium or phosphate.

page.mentor_intro: The 2026 AHA/ACC/ADA/ASN guideline frames cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome across cardiology, endocrinology and nephrology. A living guideline covers cardiovascular, kidney and weight effects of type 2 diabetes drugs, and KDIGO 2026 covers CKD anaemia. Frailty and renal dose adjustment are recurring management problems.

The 2024 KDIGO guideline establishes criteria for rapid CKD progression, defined as a sustained decline in eGFR >5 mL/min/1.73m²/year or a loss of >25% from baseline eGFR, warranting accelerated nephrology intervention.

Mandatory nephrology referral triggers include eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73m² (stages G4-G5), persistent high-grade albuminuria (uACR >300 mg/g), persistent microscopic hematuria, or a 5-year KFRE risk >3% to 5%.

The Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE) developed by Tangri et al. accurately predicts the 2-year and 5-year risk of progression to treated end-stage kidney failure using four simple variables: age, sex, eGFR, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio.

page.standard_overview: Systematic staging and risk prediction in chronic kidney disease (CKD) directs clinical decision-making regarding nephroprotective pharmacotherapy, multidisciplinary referral, and kidney failure planning. The Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) staging framework categorizes CKD across estimated GFR stages (G1 to G5) and albuminuria stages (A1 to A3). To quantify individualized risk of progression to kidney failure requiring replacement therapy (dialysis or preemptive transplant), the validated Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE)—utilizing age, sex, eGFR, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR)—provides exceptional discriminatory accuracy across global populations. Clinical guidelines recommend formal nephrology referral when the 5-year predicted kidney failure risk exceeds 3% to 5%, or when eGFR drops below 30 mL/min/1.73m² (stage G4).

page.standard_overview: Vaughan Williams Class I antiarrhythmics block cardiac voltage-gated sodium channels (Nav1.5), depressing phase 0 depolarizing upstroke velocity. Subclassified by binding kinetics and effects on action potential duration (APD): Class IA (quinidine, procainamide, disopyramide) exhibits intermediate binding kinetics and prolongs APD and QT interval; Class IB (lidocaine, mexiletine) has rapid dissociation and shortens APD; and Class IC (flecainide, propafenone) has slow dissociation, producing marked rate-dependent QRS widening without altering APD. The landmark CAST trial established that Class IC agents significantly increase mortality in structural heart disease, creating an absolute contraindication to flecainide/propafenone in ischemic heart disease, reduced LVEF, or severe LV hypertrophy. In selected patients with symptomatic atrial fibrillation and no significant structural heart disease, oral flecainide can be used for pill-in-the-pocket cardioversion with an AV-nodal blocker after efficacy and safety have first been established in a monitored setting.

page.mentor_intro: The 2025 SVS guideline on intermittent claudication stresses patient-centred assessment of risk, benefit, impairment and durability. In the CLEVER trial in aortoiliac peripheral artery disease, both supervised exercise and stenting improved peak walking time at 6 months compared with optimal medical care, and a Cochrane review shows exercise programmes improve walking time and distance in intermittent claudication.

In the COMPASS trial, rivaroxaban 2.5 mg twice daily plus aspirin reduced the primary cardiovascular outcome compared with aspirin alone (4.1% vs 5.4%; hazard ratio 0.76) with more major bleeding, and in lower-extremity PAD it lowered the incidence of major adverse limb events.

page.standard_overview: Intermittent claudication is the classic clinical manifestation of lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD), characterized by reproducible, exercise-induced muscular ache, cramp, or fatigue—most frequently in the calf, thigh, or buttock—triggered by walking and promptly relieved within 10 minutes of rest. Resting Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) <=0.90 confirms PAD, while an ABI >1.40 indicates non-compressible, calcified medial arteries requiring toe-brachial index (TBI) testing. Management has two fundamental goals: preventing systemic major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and improving functional walking distance. Comprehensive medical therapy mandates high-intensity statins, smoking cessation, and antithrombotic therapy. Structured supervised exercise therapy is a first-line functional intervention that improves walking performance; in selected aortoiliac disease, CLEVER showed greater improvement in treadmill walking time with supervised exercise than with primary stenting, although outcomes and treatment selection differ by patient.
